content.text:
You control a robot arm (a Franka Panda with a two-finger gripper) in a simulated tabletop workspace, through tools. You see the scene through a camera image and through the structured results of tools.

Rules:
- Call exactly one tool per turn, as <tool_call>{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}</tool_call>.
- Positions and sizes come from tool results (observe_scene, get_robot_state); do not estimate coordinates from the image.
- Objects are named by the tools (for example by colour); use those names in arguments.
- After acting, check the result. If an action failed, observe again and decide what to do next; do not repeat the same failing call blindly.
- If a container is closed or its mechanism is unknown, investigate_physics finds out how it moves; open_articulated opens it using what was learned.
- When the goal is achieved, call verify_goal and then finish with success=true and the goal. If the task cannot be done with these tools or this robot, call finish with success=false and explain why.

Pick up the red object and put it in the tray.
{"frame_time": 0.5000000000000003, "scene": {"objects": [{"name": "blue", "color": "blue", "position": [0.4823, -0.2631, 0.0212], "yaw": 0.768, "size": 0.0424118445168359, "visible": true, "last_seen": 0.5000000000000003, "position_std": 0.0013549770113060024}, {"name": "green", "color": "green", "position": [0.4766, -0.1551, 0.0215], "yaw": 0.297, "size": 0.04294791460676211, "visible": true, "last_seen": 0.5000000000000003, "position_std": 0.0013607040973758922}, {"name": "red", "color": "red", "position": [0.3627, -0.1927, 0.0215], "yaw": 0.454, "size": 0.04228432499771098, "visible": true, "last_seen": 0.5000000000000003, "position_std": 0.001475618759760389}], "fixtures": {"tray": {"centre": [0.5631, 0.082, 0.004], "half_width": 0.08886262311019326}}, "articulated": [], "investigations": {}, "holding": null, "holding_handle": null}, "robot": {"time": 0.5000000000000003, "joint_pos": [-0.0, 0.0, -0.0, -1.5708, 0.0, 1.5708, -0.7853], "tcp_pos": [0.5545, -0.0, 0.5211], "tcp_yaw": 1.571, "gripper_width": 0.08, "holding": null, "protective_stop": false, "capabilities": ["observe_scene", "get_robot_state", "move_end_effector", "grasp", "retract", "release", "place", "verify_goal", "investigate_physics", "open_articulated"]}}

function.name: observe_scene
function.description: List visible objects (pose estimates) and fixtures.

function.name: get_robot_state
function.description: Joint state, TCP pose, gripper state, safety status, capabilities.

function.name: grasp
function.description: Pick up a named object from above. Requires an empty gripper.

function.name: retract
function.description: Move the arm to its parking pose, clear of the workspace and of the cameras' view (to observe what the arm was hiding).

function.name: release
function.description: Open the gripper (letting go of a held handle also backs off).

function.name: place
function.description: Put the held object in a region ('tray'), on an object, or on 'table'.

function.name: verify_goal
function.description: Check a structured goal against observations, with margin.

function.name: investigate_physics
function.description: Grasp the handle of an articulated object and probe it with capped forces until its mechanism (fixed, sliding, hinged), constraint and parameters are identified, the model is found inadequate, a safety limit trips, or the probe budget is spent.

function.name: open_articulated
function.description: Open an articulated object. 'learned' (default) follows the constraint identified by investigate_physics and requires it; 'fixed_pull' pulls straight out of the front without a model (a baseline).

function.name: finish
function.description: End the task. success=true only when the goal is achieved; give the goal as a structured goal so it can be verified: {"type": "in" | "on", "object": ..., "target": ...}. Use success=false with a reason when the task is impossible, unsafe, unsupported by the robot's tools, or keeps failing.
